evidence.note: Claim: a multi-reviewer round failed to return one reviewer's finding in the review result (data['findings']), so a finding could vanish while the gate record still blocked on it. Mechanism: _finding_rows() returned a single reviewer's findings (first identifying, then after B3113b1f522 the 'named' failing reviewer) instead of every heard reviewer's. Refutation observation: a round where two secondary reviewers raise two DISTINCT findings returns only one. Probe (regression test) tests/test_review_identifying_reviewer.py::test_a_secondary_reviewers_finding_is_in_the_review_result: asserts both MEDIUM and HIGH come back; on the unfixed tree it returns only one (fails), on the fixed tree both (passes).

Rules applicable: r-bounded-everything (findings list is bounded, deduped to rows), r-evidence-over-assertion (record keeps chunk_findings evidence; result now matches), r-tests (regression test first, fails on unfixed). ddflow brief --item fixed-B-review-drops-a-reviewers-finding loaded rules.

Changed _finding_rows(results) in ddflow/api/review/records.py to return every heard reviewer's finding (status in _HEARD), and run.py to call _finding_rows(results) instead of _finding_rows(named); added regression test test_a_secondary_reviewers_finding_is_in_the_review_result (two secondary reviewers raise one MEDIUM at x.py:1, one HIGH at y.py:1; both must come back).

chunk_findings.detail: In the bug’s own multi-gate scenario (`ddflow review --gate rubber_duck,critic`), this passes the run’s combined `results` into `_finding_rows` while building a gate record for the gate represented by `named`. `_finding_rows` in `ddflow/api/review/records.py` then returns every `_HEARD` result’s findings and never filters by the reviewer’s `gates`. So a rubber_duck-only reviewer raising `FINDING LOW duck.py:1` and a critic-only reviewer raising `FINDING HIGH critic.py:1` both appear in both gate records. That makes rubber_duck triage see critic findings and vice versa. The new test only configures reviewers with `gates=["critic"]`, so it cannot catch this cross-gate contamination, even though the change is supposed to preserve each gate’s lens.

chunk_findings.detail: The `_finding_rows` function extracts every finding from all heard reviewers (`results`) and returns them in a flat list without deduplication or reviewer attribution. If two different reviewers raise findings with identical text, location, and severity (which happens frequently in consensus reviews or when reviewers analyze the same defect pattern), `rows.extend(...)` includes duplicate dictionary entries in `out.data["findings"]`. Given input where reviewers `med` and `high` both emit `FINDING MEDIUM x.py:1` with identical details, `_finding_rows` returns two identical rows, causing callers or downstream triage logic to count or process the same finding multiple times.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:144

chunk_findings.detail: The pooled list is still published as a single reviewer's work. `data["reviewer"]` and `data["family"]` stay `named`, and each finding row has no reviewer id, while `_finding_rows` now appends every heard reviewer's findings. Input: identifying pass `clean` (family google, no findings) plus secondary `med` (family xai, `FINDING MEDIUM x.py:1`) — the same shape as the new test, and as the ticket where status recorded `lan-deepseek-v4-pro` while kimi-k3's MEDIUM was the dropped row. The result is `reviewer=clean`/`family=google` with med's finding in `findings`. Anything that stores or triages by that reviewer field files kimi's finding under the wrong reviewer; a later rewrite of the named reviewer's rows can drop it again. The regression test only checks severities, so this passes.
